newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices dive $6/T, distressed sales.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices dive $6/T, distressed sales.

text.p: Battered high sulphur fuel oil prices took a further $6.00 per tonne dive on Monday amid distressed cargoes and high inventories in Hong Kong and China, traders said.
"Sellers are engaged in a price-cutting war to find buyers and refinery cuts by Shell and Esso are not helping," said a trader.

A distressed cargo for delivery between January 25-February 5 to south China was sold at $115 per tonne on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis. Bids last week into China were heard at $115 but offers were as high as $118-$119.

"Most ships and port workers in China will not be around starting January 25, they are heading back to their home provinces in time for the family reunion," he added, referring to Chinese New Year celebration in the middle of February.
Traders said there were still distressed supplies in south China.
"Two to three vessels are parked just outside China," said a trader. "Inventories in Hong Kong and China are also high."
Traders said offers were chasing bids due to the lack of buying interest in the market.
In the Singapore physical market, offers dropped sharply to just $103 in a search for buyers, compared with Friday's $108/$110.
"The Chinese market has already come to a halt," said a major. "China is the biggest buyer here and if they stop buying, prices definitely come underpressure," he said.

Discussions were also heard that some Chinese buyers have reneged on earlier purchases. Traders said plunging fuel oil prices have caused these buyers to "flake" on the more expensive purchases, done before the price fall that started January 6.

Traders said majors were trying to dispose of their cargoes in the bunker market in order to "make space" for the incoming supplies from Mideast. Bunker values also plummeted under selling pressure with 380-cst seen at $104 down at least $3 from Friday.
In the swaps market, the February/March time swaps slipped into contango late afternoon with a spread traded at minus 75 cents.
Only offers were seen in the paper market late in the day.
